Ekipman gereksinimi kümülatiftir: A3 gem: The equipment requirement is cumulative: an A3 ship also carries the A1 and A2 equipment. Every ship also carries an EPIRB, a SART and portable VHF radios (for survival craft). The equipment is chosen according to the ship's farthest operating area.
Denizcilik emniyet bilgisi (MSI) — seyir: Maritime safety information (MSI) — navigational warnings, weather reports, SAR information — is received automatically. NAVTEX (518 kHz) provides MSI in coastal waters and Inmarsat SafetyNET in the open sea (A3/A4). These broadcasts are received and recorded continuously and automatically.
GMDSS, ana güç kaybında bile çalışmalıdı: The GMDSS must work even when main power is lost; a separate battery (reserve source of energy) therefore supplies the GMDSS equipment for a set time (typically 1–6 hours, depending on the configuration). Availability of the equipment is ensured by duplication or shore-based maintenance.
GMDSS ekipmanını yetkili operatör (GOC/R: The GMDSS equipment is operated by an authorised operator (holding a GOC/ROC certificate). Periodic tests (daily/weekly/monthly) according to the maintenance method are carried out and a radio log is kept. If a false distress alert is sent, it is cancelled at once.
VHF deniz bandı belirli kanallara ayrılm: The VHF maritime band is divided into specific channels. Channel 16 (156.8 MHz) is the distress, safety and calling channel; a continuous watch is kept on it. Channel 70 is for DSC (not used for voice). Channel 13 is for bridge-to-bridge (safety of navigation), channel 06 for ship-to-ship, and the other channels for port/VTS and general communications.
Simpleks kanalda aynı frekansta sırayla: On a simplex channel the parties speak in turn on the same frequency (ship-to-ship); a duplex channel uses two frequencies (telephone connection). The output power can be set to high (25 W) or low (1 W); low power is preferred for short-range communication and to avoid unnecessary interference.
DSC distress butonu (korumalı kapak altı: The DSC distress button (under a protective cover) sends the MMSI, the position (if a GPS is connected) and the nature of distress on channel 70 with a single action. When the alert is received, the stations concerned give an automatic alarm and voice follow-up takes place on channel 16. The alert is sent by holding the button down for 4–5 seconds.
VHF görüş hattı (line of sight) ile çalı: VHF works by line of sight; the range depends on the antenna height. A higher antenna gives a longer range. The antenna position is chosen taking into account shadowing and interference with other antennas. A damaged antenna or coaxial cable seriously reduces the range.
Filika/sallarda kullanılmak üzere taşına: Portable GMDSS VHF radios (generally yellow or orange and waterproof) are carried for use in lifeboats and liferafts; they provide communication with SAR units and the ship during a rescue. They have separate (spare) batteries and are tested regularly.
Bakım; basınç göstergesi (manometre) kon: Maintenance covers checking the pressure gauge, the integrity of the seal and pin, weighing (CO₂), checking the hose, nozzle and extinguisher shell for corrosion, and periodic pressure testing (hydrostatic test) and recharging. Each unit is labelled and recorded.
Günlük DSC testi (kıyı/başka istasyonla: The daily DSC test (with a coast station or another station, or a self-test), antenna and coaxial cable checks, and battery and portable VHF tests are carried out, and the radio log is kept. Care is taken not to press the real distress button by mistake during the test.
Lifeboat gemiyi terk etmek (çok kişiyi u: A lifeboat is for abandoning ship (taking many people away); a rescue boat is for active rescue — reaching a person in the water and marshalling liferafts. A rescue boat must therefore be fast, highly manoeuvrable and easy and quick to launch. On some ships a lifeboat is also approved as the rescue boat.
FRB genelde sertgövde-şişme (RIB) yapıda: A fast rescue boat (FRB) is usually a rigid-inflatable (RIB), driven by an outboard motor or a waterjet. A waterjet reduces the risk of propeller injuries in shallow water and when recovering people. The FRB must be fast (to manoeuvre in bad weather) and self-righting.
FRB davit'i, botu kötü havada bile hızlı: The FRB davit must be able to launch the boat quickly even in bad weather and — critically — recover it quickly while the ship is under way or in a seaway. A constant-tension, shock-absorbing winch system damps the sudden load difference between the boat and the ship during recovery. Recovery is the most difficult and dangerous part of a man overboard response.
MOB durumunda: alarm + can simidi/duman: In a man overboard situation the steps are: alarm and throwing a lifebuoy and smoke signal, turning back with a manoeuvre (Williamson/Anderson turn), posting lookouts, preparing and launching the rescue boat, picking up the person and returning to the ship. If the water is cold, time is critical because of hypothermia; a fast response saves lives.
Rescue boat/FRB ekibi düzenli eğitim ve: The rescue boat/FRB crew trains and drills regularly; SOLAS requires a specially trained crew for the FRB and periodic launching and manoeuvring drills. Protective clothing for cold water (immersion/exposure suits) is provided for the crew.
Bakım; motor/su jeti çalıştırma testi, y: Maintenance covers running tests of the engine or waterjet, fuel and battery, the pressure and condition of the inflatable tubes (RIB), the davit winch and constant-tension system, and the release and equipment. The boat is always kept ready for quick launching.
MF (yaklaşık 1.6-4 MHz) gündüz ground wa: MF (about 1.6–4 MHz) gives a range of about 150–300 miles by day through the ground wave; at night the range increases through the sky wave. HF (3–30 MHz) reaches thousands of miles, even global range, by reflection from the ionosphere (sky wave); but the range varies with the frequency, the time of day and ionospheric conditions.
MF DSC tehlike frekansı 2187.5 kHz'tir;: The MF DSC distress frequency is 2187.5 kHz; on HF there are separate DSC distress frequencies in the 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 MHz bands. The distress alert is sent by DSC on a suitable frequency and received automatically by the coast station. Radiotelephony and NBDP (telex) distress frequencies are also defined.
DSC ile çağrı kurulduktan sonra sesli (R: Once a call has been set up by DSC, the content is passed by voice (RT) or by NBDP (Narrow Band Direct Printing/telex). NBDP transmits text reliably in the noisy HF environment. After a distress alert the coast station mostly follows up by voice.
MF/HF, uzun tel/whip anten ve otomatik a: MF/HF sets are matched to the different frequencies with a long wire or whip antenna and an automatic antenna tuner (ATU). A good RF earth (ground) system (hull/sea earth) determines efficiency; a poor earth reduces range and output power. An ATU fault prevents transmission on certain bands.
A2 gemisi MF DSC taşır; A4 (kutup) gemis: An A2 ship carries MF DSC; HF DSC is mandatory for an A4 (polar) ship because the Inmarsat GEO satellites give no coverage at the poles. A3 ships may also carry MF/HF as an alternative or back-up to Inmarsat.
Günlük/haftalık DSC testi, anten/tuner v: Daily and weekly DSC tests, checks of the antenna, tuner and earth system, battery tests and the radio log are carried out. The test is made not on the actual distress frequency but with the appropriate test procedure.
Inmarsat-C, jeostatik (GEO) uydular üzer: Inmarsat-C works through geostationary (GEO) satellites; the ship terminal connects to the satellite and the satellite to a land earth station (LES). The NCS (Network Coordination Station) manages network traffic. GEO satellites cover the area between about 70°N and 70°S (A3); the poles (A4) are outside coverage.
Inmarsat-C gerçek zamanlı ses taşımaz; m: Inmarsat-C does not carry real-time voice; it packages messages and sends and receives them by the store-and-forward method. A low data rate is sufficient because it is designed for distress alerts and telex/email-type text. The antenna is small and omnidirectional (it needs no pointing).
Korumalı distress butonu, GPS konumu ve: The protected distress button sends the distress alert, with the GPS position and the ship's identity, through the selected LES to the relevant MRCC (Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre). Because the alert includes the nature of distress and the position, SAR can be started quickly.
EGC (Enhanced Group Call) üzerinden Safe: Through EGC (Enhanced Group Call), the SafetyNET service delivers navigational warnings, weather forecasts and SAR information to the ship automatically in the open sea (A3); FleetNET is for commercial group messages. These MSI broadcasts are received and recorded automatically; they are the open-sea complement to NAVTEX.
A3 gemisi GMDSS yedekliliğini Inmarsat +: An A3 ship provides GMDSS redundancy with a combination of Inmarsat + MF/HF or with dual Inmarsat. The GMDSS is now becoming multi-provider; low-earth-orbit (LEO) systems such as Iridium offer global coverage including the poles and can also meet A4 requirements.
Performans testi (LES üzerinden), anten: The performance test (via an LES), checks of the antenna line of sight and cabling, the GPS input, verification of EGC reception and a test of the reserve battery are carried out. It is monitored that EGC messages are received without interruption.
EPIRB aktive olunca 406 MHz'de dijital t: When activated, the EPIRB transmits a digital distress signal on 406 MHz; this signal is received by the Cospas-Sarsat satellites (LEO + GEO + MEOSAR) and relayed to ground stations (LUTs). The digital message contains the unique identity of the ship (hex ID/MMSI); the position is determined by the internal GPS or by Doppler. A 121.5 MHz homing signal also guides SAR units.
EPIRB, float-free braket içinde dış güve: The EPIRB is stowed on the open deck in a float-free bracket. If the ship sinks, the hydrostatic release unit (HRU) cuts the lashing at a certain depth of water (about 1.5–4 m); the EPIRB floats to the surface and activates automatically on contact with water. Manual activation is also possible.
HRU'nun son kullanma tarihi vardır (gene: The HRU has an expiry date (generally 2 years) and is replaced on time; an expired HRU may not release. The EPIRB battery and mounting bracket are also checked periodically.
EPIRB, gemi ve irtibat bilgileriyle ilgi: The EPIRB must be registered with the relevant authority with the ship's and contact details. Correct registration lets SAR identify the ship quickly, reach the owner and distinguish a real alarm from a false one. The registration is updated when the ship or the owner changes.
Bakım; self-test fonksiyonu (gerçek yayı: Maintenance covers the self-test function (without a real transmission), the battery and HRU expiry dates, and checks of the bracket, mounting and casing. Annual and periodic (shore-based) inspections are carried out. No real distress transmission is sent during a test.
Radar-SART, 9 GHz (X-band) arama radarın: When a radar SART receives the pulse of a 9 GHz (X-band) search radar, it sends a series of response pulses on the same frequency; on the radar screen this appears as a line of 12 dots (blips) extending outwards from the SART. As the distance closes, the dots become arcs. This pattern clearly shows the position of the SART.
AIS-SART, radar yerine AIS üzerinden çal: An AIS-SART works through AIS instead of radar: it transmits the position from its internal GPS as a special AIS message; the position of the SART appears as a symbol on the AIS display of nearby ships. It is an alternative or complement to the radar SART and gives the position numerically.
Menzil yüksekliğe bağlıdır; SART ne kada: The range depends on height; the higher the SART is held (e.g. raised on a pole in the liferaft), the greater the range. It is typically detected at about 8 miles from a ship and much farther from an aircraft. Close to the water surface the range of the SART falls.
Gemi terk edilirken SART filikaya/sala a: When abandoning ship, the SART is taken into the lifeboat or liferaft and activated; it is held as high as possible. An activated SART helps SAR units find the survival craft by radar and AIS. The SART is kept on the bridge in an easily accessible, portable position.
Bakım; batarya son kullanma tarihi, self: Maintenance covers the battery expiry date, the self-test (test mode near a radar), checks of the casing and watertightness, and the bracket. The test is carried out with the maker's test procedure without a real SAR transmission.
BNWAS belirli bir süre (dormant period,: The BNWAS waits for a reset (movement or button) from the officer within a set time (the dormant period, adjustable at about 3–12 minutes). When the time runs out, it first gives an audible and visual warning on the bridge; if the officer still does not respond, an alarm sounds in the cabins of the Master and the back-up officers; finally a general alarm may be given throughout the ship. In this way the officer's condition is safeguarded.
Reset, köprüdeki reset butonu veya harek: The reset is made with the reset button on the bridge or with motion detectors; the officer's physical presence on the bridge is detected. The reset cannot be made from outside the bridge; this prevents anyone silencing it remotely.
BNWAS modları: Automatic (otopilot/seyir: BNWAS modes: Automatic (activated automatically with the autopilot or when under way), Manual ON (always on) and OFF. Selecting OFF and setting the dormant period are restricted to the Master (password or key protected); the officer cannot switch it off at will. It is usually activated automatically when the ship is under way.
BNWAS özellikle otopilotta (kimse aktif: The BNWAS is particularly important on autopilot (when no one is actively steering), because the risk of falling asleep increases while the officer is passively monitoring. The system can be set to activate automatically when the autopilot is engaged.
Bakım; alarm kademelerinin fonksiyon tes: Maintenance covers function testing of the alarm stages, the motion sensors and reset button, the cabin alarm speakers and the power supply. The test verifies that the real chain of stages (bridge → cabins → ship) works.
VDR; köprü sesi (mikrofonlar), VHF haber: The VDR records, with time stamps, bridge audio (microphones), VHF communications, the radar/ECDIS picture, position, speed and heading, depth, helm and engine orders, alarms, wind and other sensors. This multi-source record allows the moment of an accident to be reconstructed.
Veriler, yangın ve derin basınç/çarpmaya: The data is stored in a protective recording medium (protective capsule) resistant to fire, deep-water pressure and impact. Modern VDRs have both a fixed capsule (recovered if the ship sinks) and a float-free capsule (which floats to the surface and transmits a signal like an EPIRB). The float-free capsule makes it easier to recover data from a sunken ship.
VDR son belirli süreyi (kapsülde tipik e: The VDR keeps the most recent period (typically at least 48 hours in the capsule, longer in internal memory under modern standards), continuously overwriting it (loop). After an accident or significant event this loop must be stopped and the data preserved (save/lock); otherwise it is overwritten.
S-VDR (Simplified), tam VDR'ye göre daha: The S-VDR (Simplified VDR) records less data than a full VDR (for example the radar picture may not be mandatory); it was used on existing (retrofit) ships for reasons of cost. A full VDR is standard on new ships.
VDR yılda bir APT (Annual Performance Te: The VDR is tested once a year by an authorised service in the APT (Annual Performance Test) and a certificate of compliance is issued. After an accident, the Master must stop the recording to prevent the data being overwritten, preserve the data and hand it over to the authorities.
Bakım; APT, mikrofon/ses kanalı kontrolü: Maintenance covers the APT, checks of the microphones and audio channels, correct recording of the sensor inputs (radar, GPS, gyro), the condition of the capsule, the battery (reserve power) and the expiry date of the float-free HRU.
Modern gemilerde tamamen kapalı (totally: On modern ships totally enclosed lifeboats are standard; they are fire- and watertight, self-righting and motorised. Free-fall lifeboats are launched into the sea down a ramp at the stern; they give fast evacuation and are common on bulk carriers and tankers. Tankers may require fire-protected lifeboats.
Gravity davit, filikayı kendi ağırlığıyl: A gravity davit lowers the lifeboat out and down by its own weight (with a brake); it is the most common type. A free-fall davit lets the lifeboat drop freely and uses a separate winch for recovery. The davit must be strong enough to carry the weight of the fully loaded lifeboat safely.
Filika kancası (release hook); off-load: The lifeboat release hook may be off-load (opens only without load, when the boat is waterborne) or on-load (can open under load, before the boat is waterborne). On-load release allows quick release but, if misused, can make the lifeboat fall from height. Interlocks and a hydrostatic interlock (which prevents opening before the boat is waterborne) are therefore important.
Mürettebat embarkasyon güvertesinde fili: The crew board the lifeboat at the embarkation deck; when the davit brake is released, the lifeboat descends under control. The brake (centrifugal/band brake) limits the speed of lowering. When the boat is waterborne, the release is opened and the boat moves away from the ship on the painter. The whole procedure must be known thoroughly from drills.
SOLAS, filikaların düzenli denize indiri: SOLAS requires lifeboats to be launched regularly and their engines run; the davit brake, winch and release system are subject to periodic load tests. Abandon ship drills are held regularly; the crew know their duties and stations (muster list).
Filika; SOLAS donanımı (kürek, işaret fi: The lifeboat is fitted with SOLAS equipment (oars, pyrotechnics, first aid, water and food, compass, SART/VHF, painter). It is checked regularly that these items are complete and within their expiry dates.
Bakım; davit winch/fren, tel halat (fall: Maintenance covers the davit winch and brake, wear and the renewal period of the falls, the release mechanism and hydrostatic interlock, the engine and battery, hull integrity and the expiry dates of the equipment. The falls are turned end for end or renewed at set intervals.
Throw-over (atılır) liferaft, kapsül (ca: A throw-over liferaft is stowed on deck in a canister; when thrown into the sea, it inflates when the painter is pulled. A davit-launched liferaft is boarded from the ship and lowered by davit; it reduces the risk of jumping into the water from a high-sided ship. Both work on the same inflation principle.
Painter (bağlama halatı) belirli uzunluk: When the painter is pulled out to a certain length, it opens the valve of the gas cylinder; the CO₂/nitrogen mixture inflates the raft within seconds and the canister splits in two. If the raft inflates upside down, one person can right it with the righting strap. After inflation the painter stays attached to the ship; once the raft is boarded it is cut or released.
HRU, liferaft kapsülünü krezete (cradle): The HRU automatically cuts the lashing that secures the liferaft canister to its cradle when the sinking ship reaches a certain depth of water (about 1.5–4 m), by water pressure. The canister is freed and floats to the surface; as the painter is still attached to the ship, the raft inflates automatically.
Painter, gemiye bir weak link (zayıf bağ: The painter is attached to the ship through a weak link. If the ship continues to sink after the raft has inflated and is floating, the weak link breaks at a certain load and saves the raft from being dragged down with the sinking ship. The weak link must be strong enough for the raft to stay attached to the ship and inflate, but weak enough not to follow the sinking ship.
Liferaft, içindeki SOLAS donanım paketiy: The liferaft comes with a SOLAS equipment pack inside (A or B pack: pyrotechnics, water, food, first aid, paddles, lifeline, sponges, repair kit). The capacity (number of persons) is marked on the canister; the total capacity of the rafts and lifeboats on board must cover everyone on board.
Liferaft, yetkili servis istasyonunda pe: The liferaft is opened, inflated, pressure-tested, re-equipped and repacked periodically (generally annually, extended for some systems) at an approved service station. The HRU expiry date (generally 2 years) is followed and the HRU replaced on time.
Gemide bakım; kapsül/cradle bütünlüğü, H: Maintenance on board covers the integrity of the canister and cradle, correct fitting of the HRU and weak link, the painter attachment, the last service and HRU dates, and the lashing. Internal servicing is carried out only at an approved station.
İki zamanlı çevrimde her krank dönüşünde: In the two-stroke cycle one power stroke is produced for every revolution of the crankshaft: compression as the piston rises, fuel injection and combustion at the top, the power stroke as it descends, and scavenging and exhaust at the bottom. Modern large engines use uniflow scavenging: scavenge air enters through ports at the bottom of the liner and the exhaust leaves through a single exhaust valve in the cylinder cover; this gives a clean charge and high efficiency.
Pervane verimi düşük devirde ve büyük ça: Propeller efficiency is high at low speed and large diameter. The two-stroke engine runs directly at this speed, eliminating gearbox losses. A large stroke/bore ratio (ultra-long stroke) raises the thermal efficiency above 50%.
Ana parçalar: silindir gömleği (liner),: The main parts: cylinder liner, piston and piston rings, piston rod, crosshead, connecting rod, crankshaft and main bearings. The crosshead design separates the side thrust from the liner; this reduces liner wear and allows the cylinder lubrication to be managed separately.
Piston rod, silindir alanı ile karter (c: The piston rod passes between the cylinder space and the crankcase through the stuffing box. This prevents the dirty cylinder oil from mixing with the clean crankcase oil. The cylinder oil (high BN, a separate system) and the system/crankcase oil are independent.
Geleneksel motorlarda yakıt pompası ve e: In conventional engines the fuel pumps and exhaust valves are driven by the camshaft. In modern electronically controlled engines (MAN ME, WinGD RT-flex), a high-pressure common rail fuel system and hydraulic servo optimise injection timing and valve movement for each load and speed; the camshaft is eliminated.
Egzoz gazı turboşarjı çevirir; kompresör: The exhaust gas drives the turbocharger; the compressor delivers the scavenge air, the air cooler cools and densifies the compressed air, and it is fed to the cylinders through the scavenge air receiver. At low load the auxiliary blowers start to provide enough air.
Silindir yağı, gömleğe ölçülü dozlarla (: Cylinder oil is fed to the liner in metered doses (cylinder lubricators / Alpha lubrication); the base number (BN) of the oil is chosen according to the sulphur content of the fuel, to neutralise it. In MARPOL Annex VI Tier III areas, EGR or SCR is used for NOx, and low-sulphur fuel or a scrubber for SOx.
Silindir başına egzoz sıcaklığı, maksimu: The exhaust temperature of each cylinder, the maximum combustion pressure (Pmax), the scavenge air pressure and temperature, the turbocharger speed and the bearing temperatures are monitored continuously. An imbalance (one cylinder deviating) points to a problem with an injector, a valve or the load distribution.
Çevrim dört stroktan oluşur: emme (intak: The cycle consists of four strokes: intake, compression, power and exhaust. One power stroke is produced every two crankshaft revolutions (720°). The intake and exhaust valves are timed by the camshaft; valve overlap allows the cylinder to be scavenged with fresh air and increases turbocharger efficiency.
Dört zamanlı motor daha yüksek devirde (: The four-stroke engine runs at a higher speed (about 500–1000 rpm), uses a trunk piston (no crosshead) and is lubricated by a single oil circuit (common to the cylinders and the crankcase). Its power density is high; but for propelling large ships it is usually combined with a gearbox or electric propulsion.
Orta devirli motorlar MDO/MGO ile çalışa: Medium-speed engines can run on MDO/MGO and can also burn HFO with heating and viscosity control. Generator engines can change over to light fuel (MGO) during manoeuvring and in port. Heating the fuel to the correct viscosity (about 10–15 cSt at injection) is critical for atomisation and efficiency.
Jeneratör motorlarında sabit devir (frek: Generator engines need a constant speed (frequency); the governor therefore keeps the speed constant by adjusting the fuel as the load changes. On propulsion engines the governor sets the speed according to the operator's command. With generators in parallel, load sharing is managed through the governor droop setting.
Egzozla çevrilen turboşarj, emme havasın: The exhaust-driven turbocharger compresses the intake air; the intercooler (charge air cooler) cools the air, increasing its density and reducing NOx. Charge air temperature and pressure are direct indicators of performance.
Bakım; supap klerans ayarı, enjektör tes: Maintenance covers setting valve clearances, testing injectors, measuring piston ring and liner wear, checking bearing clearances, cleaning the turbocharger and coolers and changing oil and fuel filters. The PMS is applied according to running hours.
Şaft hattı, makineden pervaneye doğru sı: From the engine to the propeller, the shaft line consists of the thrust shaft, the intermediate shaft(s) and the propeller (tail) shaft. They are joined by flanged couplings. The tail shaft passes through the stern tube and carries the propeller.
Pervane itkisi (ileri/geri) şaft üzerind: The propeller thrust (ahead or astern) is transmitted through the shaft to the thrust block, which transfers this axial force to the hull (seating) and moves the ship ahead or astern. Tilting-pad thrust bearings run on an oil film; their temperature and oil flow are monitored.
The tail shaft turns in the stern tube bearing. The conventional system is oil-lubricated (white metal bearing, pressure from a gravity tank). The environmentally friendly alternative is a water-lubricated system (composite or lignum vitae bearings); it eliminates the risk of oil leakage, but bearing wear is monitored differently.
Stern tube seal (örn. lip seal/Simplex),: The stern tube seal (e.g. lip seal/Simplex type) prevents seawater from entering and oil from escaping around the shaft. The spaces between the multiple lip rings are fed with oil. Seal wear causes oil leakage (pollution of the sea) or water ingress (bearing damage).
Şaft hattı, gövde deformasyonu ve sıcakl: The shaft line is aligned so that the bearings are loaded evenly despite hull deflection and temperature (bearing reactions / sag and gap). Wrong alignment leads to bearing overload, heating and vibration. The alignment is measured at the shipyard and verified under service conditions when necessary.
Şaft hattının burulma (torsional) ve eği: The torsional and bending (whirling) natural frequencies of the shaft line must not create resonance within the engine speed range. Certain speed ranges may be barred (barred speed range); the engine is not run continuously in this range.
Tail shaft, klas tarafından periyodik su: The tail shaft is subject to periodic class survey (withdrawal or an in-place condition monitoring programme). Stern tube oil analysis (water and metal content), seal checks, bearing temperature and shaft position (poker gauge/wear-down) measurements are carried out regularly.
Pitch (hatve), pervanenin bir tam dönüşt: Pitch is the distance the propeller should theoretically advance in one full revolution. The diameter, number of blades and blade area ratio (BAR) determine thrust and efficiency. A large diameter and low speed increase efficiency; the number of blades affects vibration and cavitation.
FPP (Fixed Pitch Propeller) sabit hatvel: An FPP (fixed pitch propeller) has a fixed pitch; for manoeuvring and going astern the engine reverses. A CPP (controllable pitch propeller) adjusts thrust and direction at constant speed by changing the blade angle; it gives high manoeuvrability and suits a shaft generator, but it is mechanically complex and expensive.
Slip, teorik ilerleme (pitch × devir) il: Slip is the difference between the theoretical advance (pitch × revolutions) and the actual advance. Apparent slip is calculated with the GPS speed, real slip with the actual speed through the water. Slip rising above normal points to hull fouling, weather or current, or propeller damage.
Pervane yükü tahmininde \"propeller law\: The "propeller law" is used to estimate the propeller load: torque ~ speed², power ~ speed³. Increasing speed a little therefore increases the power demand by the cube. A fouled hull or heavy weather makes the propeller heavy; the engine reaches the same speed with more fuel (heavy running).
Kanat üzerindeki basınç buhar basıncının: When the pressure on the blade falls below the vapour pressure, the water turns into vapour bubbles (cavitation); the bubbles collapse in the high-pressure region, eroding the blade surface (erosion), producing noise and vibration and reducing efficiency. Overloading, a damaged blade or a wrong pitch increases cavitation.
Havuzlamada pervane yüzeyi parlatılır (p: During dry-docking the propeller surface is polished (for efficiency), damage to the blade edges is repaired and the balance is checked. On a CPP the hub sealing and the pitch mechanism are tested. The rope guard and the propeller boss are checked.
Dümen, dönme ekseni ile yüzey alanının d: Rudders are classified by the position of the turning axis relative to the area: balanced (spade/balanced), semi-balanced and unbalanced. In a balanced rudder the axis divides the area, so the turning moment (torque) is reduced. A flap (Becker) rudder gives extra lift at large rudder angles with its trailing flap (high manoeuvrability).
Dümeni çeviren güç hidroliktir. Ram tipi: The power that turns the rudder is hydraulic. In the ram type, cylinders push the tiller; in the rotary vane type, vanes attached to the rudder stock turn under pressure. The pumps (usually two, variable delivery) drive the rudder to the ordered angle.
Ana dümen donanımı, gemi tam yüklü ve se: The main steering gear must be able to put the rudder over from 35° on one side to 30° on the other side in not more than 28 seconds with the ship at its deepest draft and at maximum service speed. The auxiliary steering gear must be able to do 15° to 15° in 60 seconds (at half speed). These criteria are the foundation of safe manoeuvring.
Dümen kontrolü köprüden iki bağımsız sis: It must be possible to control the steering from the bridge through two independent systems; if the main system fails, it must be possible to change over to the auxiliary from the bridge, and local (emergency) control must be available in the steering gear compartment. On tankers, steering capability must be maintained after a single failure (single failure criterion).
Köprüdeki dümen komutu, telemotor (eski: The helm order on the bridge is transmitted to the steering gear compartment by the telemotor (older hydraulic or modern electric). In follow-up mode the rudder stops at the ordered angle; in non-follow-up mode it moves for as long as the button is held. The autopilot corrects the rudder automatically according to the course error.
Dümen etkisi pervane akımına bağlıdır; p: Rudder effect depends on the propeller wash; when the propeller stops, the rudder loses effect. Manoeuvring parameters such as transverse thrust (the propeller's sideways effect), the pivot point and advance/transfer must be known by the bridge team. As the rudder angle increases, stall (flow separation) and loss of speed occur.
Bakım; hidrolik yağ seviyesi/analizi, sı: Maintenance covers the hydraulic oil level and analysis, leak checks, ram or vane seals, the rudder stock bearing and carrier bearing, the feedback linkage and the safety and limit settings. Regular testing and alarm checks are mandatory.
Radar, anten üzerinden çok kısa süreli y: The radar transmits very short, high-power microwave pulses through the antenna. A pulse strikes a target and returns; the range is calculated from the round-trip time (R = c·t/2) and the bearing from the direction of the antenna. On the screen the own ship is at the centre and targets are shown against the range rings.
X-band (~9 GHz, 3 cm) yüksek çözünürlük: X-band (~9 GHz, 3 cm) gives high resolution and detection of small targets but is affected by rain; SARTs and racons are detected on X-band. S-band (~3 GHz, 10 cm) penetrates rain and fog better and is stable at long range. SOLAS V/19 requires ships of 3000 GT and above to have a second radar in addition to the 9 GHz radar (a 3 GHz/S-band radar or, where the Administration considers it appropriate, a second 9 GHz/X-band radar); the two radars must be able to work independently of each other.
ARPA, seçilen veya otomatik kazanılan he: ARPA tracks selected or automatically acquired targets and calculates their speed and course vectors and their CPA (Closest Point of Approach) and TCPA (Time to CPA). Vectors can be shown in true or relative mode; the relative vector is used to judge risk of collision, the true vector to understand the target's actual movement.
ARPA trial (deneme) manevrası, planlanan: The ARPA trial manoeuvre simulates the new CPA/TCPA with all tracked targets for a planned change of course or speed. It is used to check that the manoeuvre is sufficient and early, but the delay time must be set realistically.
Deniz yüzeyinden (sea clutter) ve yağmur: Echoes from the sea surface (sea clutter) and rain (rain clutter) can mask real targets. The sea clutter (STC/anti-clutter sea) and rain clutter (FTC/anti-clutter rain) controls suppress this noise; but excessive suppression can also remove small real targets.
Yan loblar (side echoes), çok yollu yans: Side lobe echoes, multiple and indirect echoes, shadow sectors and interference (from other radars) lead to misinterpretation. Recognising these artefacts is essential for reading the screen correctly.
SOLAS V/19, tonaja göre bir veya iki rad: SOLAS V/19 requires one or two radars depending on tonnage (the second normally S-band). The performance monitor (PM) is used to check the transmitter power and receiver sensitivity on the screen; tuning and the PM are checked regularly.
ENC (Electronic Navigational Chart), vek: An ENC (Electronic Navigational Chart) is an official, vector-based, layered and "intelligent" chart; its objects can be queried and can generate alarms. An RNC (Raster Navigational Chart) is a scanned image of a paper chart; it has no intelligence and is used only in RCDS mode with an appropriate folio of paper charts. Full ECDIS compliance requires ENCs.
ENC'ler S-63 standardıyla şifrelenir; ge: ENCs are encrypted with the S-63 standard; the ship receives cell permits and weekly updates through a subscription. Loading the updates regularly is mandatory for legal and safety reasons; an out-of-date chart creates liability for a navigational accident.
ECDIS; GNSS (konum), gyro (heading), log: The ECDIS receives data from the GNSS (position), gyro (heading), log (speed), radar/ARPA (targets), AIS, echo sounder (depth) and the track-steering system. The accuracy of the position source (e.g. a GPS failure) directly affects navigational safety; an alarm is given when sensors are inconsistent.
ECDIS tek arıza noktası olmamalıdır. SOL: The ECDIS must not be a single point of failure. SOLAS requires a second ECDIS with an independent power supply (back-up ECDIS) or an appropriate folio of paper charts. The back-up system must be able to continue navigation without interruption if the main unit fails.
Safety contour (emniyet konturu), gemini: The safety contour is the safe depth limit for the ship's draft; the ECDIS highlights this contour and gives an alarm if it is crossed. The safety depth and the shallow and deep contour settings determine the colour coding. The guard zone / look-ahead warns in advance if there is a safety contour or a dangerous object ahead.
Planlanan rota, ECDIS'in otomatik rota k: The planned route is scanned against the safety settings with the ECDIS's automatic route check function; legs that cross the contour, contain a dangerous object or go outside the XTD are flagged. This check must also be verified visually on the bridge.
Yanlış ayarlanmış emniyet parametreleri: Wrongly set safety parameters produce a large number of unnecessary alarms; this "alarm fatigue" causes a real danger to be missed. The parameters are set carefully for the ship's draft and the navigation area, and alarms are not silenced at will.
Sınıf A AIS, SOLAS gemilerinde zorunludu: Class A AIS is mandatory on SOLAS ships; it transmits more often, at high power (12.5 W) and with SOTDMA access. Class B has lower power, transmits less often and is intended for non-commercial and small craft. Class A sees Class B but has priority.
AIS üç tür bilgi yayınlar: statik (IMO n: AIS transmits three types of information: static (IMO number, call sign, name, dimensions), dynamic (position, COG, SOG, heading, ROT) and voyage-related (draft, type of cargo, destination, ETA). Static and voyage data are entered manually; a wrong entry broadcasts wrong information.
AIS, iki özel VHF kanalında (AIS 1 / AIS: AIS works on two dedicated VHF channels (AIS 1 / AIS 2) and divides time into 2250 slots per minute. With SOTDMA (Self-Organising Time Division Multiple Access) each station chooses a free slot and avoids collisions; the network organises itself and needs no central control.
AIS yalnızca AIS taşıyan ve cihazı açık: AIS shows only targets that carry AIS with the equipment switched on; it does not see craft without AIS, land or other objects. The primary means of collision avoidance is therefore radar; AIS is complementary. Before manoeuvring on the basis of an AIS target, it must be verified by radar or by sight.
AIS, hedefin gerçek rota/hızını verdiği: Because AIS gives the target's actual course and speed, it supports the assessment of CPA/TCPA; but AIS data may be delayed or wrong. Manoeuvring decisions under COLREG are taken after confirmation with radar/ARPA.
300 GT üstü uluslararası sefer ve 500 GT: Ships of 300 GT and above on international voyages, all ships of 500 GT and above, and passenger ships carry AIS. AIS is kept switched on at all times; however, the Master has the authority to switch it off for safety reasons (e.g. in a piracy area), and this is recorded.
GPS alıcısı, en az dört uydudan gelen si: A GPS receiver measures the travel time of signals from at least four satellites. Trilateration is done with the known position of each satellite and the range calculated from the signal time (pseudorange); three satellites give the position and the fourth resolves the receiver clock error. As the signal travels at the speed of light, timing at the nanosecond level is needed.
Konum hatasına iyonosferik/troposferik g: Ionospheric and tropospheric delay, satellite orbit and clock errors, multipath (reflection from structures or the water surface) and receiver noise contribute to the position error. The total of these errors is of the order of a few metres for standard GPS.
DOP (Dilution of Precision), uyduların g: DOP (Dilution of Precision) is the effect of the distribution of the satellites in the sky on accuracy. If the satellites are close together (poor geometry), HDOP rises and the position error grows. The receiver usually gives a warning when HDOP is high.
DGPS (Differential GPS), konumu bilinen: DGPS (Differential GPS) works by a shore reference station at a known position broadcasting the error it measures; by applying this correction, the ship improves the accuracy from a few metres to sub-metre level. IALA radio beacons and SBAS (e.g. EGNOS/WAAS) provide this correction.
GNSS sinyali çok zayıf olduğundan karışt: Because the GNSS signal is very weak, it is open to jamming (drowning the signal) and spoofing (a false signal giving a wrong position). In certain areas, loss of GPS or a sudden jump in position may be a sign of spoofing; independent positioning (radar fix, terrestrial methods, dual GNSS) is then used.
İki bağımsız GNSS alıcısı, dead reckonin: Two independent GNSS receivers, dead reckoning (DR) capability and the skill to take terrestrial fixes provide redundancy. If GNSS is lost, the officer must be able to continue navigating by DR and radar or visual fixes.
Gyro pusula, yüksek hızda dönen bir roto: The gyrocompass uses the conservation of angular momentum of a rotor spinning at high speed (gyroscopic inertia) and its interaction with the earth's rotation (precession). With a gravity and damping arrangement, the rotor axis seeks true north (north-seeking) and stays there (north-settling). This gives a true north reference independent of the magnetic field.
Gyro pusula bazı sistematik hatalar göst: The gyrocompass shows some systematic errors: latitude (damping) error, speed/course/latitude error (the deviation caused by the ship's speed and latitude) and ballistic deflection during manoeuvres. Modern gyros correct these automatically, but the principle must be known.
Manyetik pusula manyetik kuzeyi gösterir: The magnetic compass points to magnetic north. The angle between true north and magnetic north is the variation, taken from the chart with its annual change. The error caused by the ship's own magnetic field is the deviation; it changes with the ship's heading and the cargo, and is given for each compass heading by the deviation card.
Compass → True dönüşümünde sapma ve deği: In converting from compass to true, deviation and variation are applied in turn. The rule for adding or subtracting easterly (E) errors must be memorised; the classic mnemonic "CADET — Compass ADd East (to get True)" is used. The compass error is measured regularly by the azimuth of celestial bodies (sun or stars) or by a transit of two objects.
Gyro heading; köprü repeater'ları, dümen: The gyro heading is distributed to the bridge repeaters, the steering, radar/ECDIS, AIS and the autopilot. The repeaters must follow the master gyro exactly; if there is a difference, the synchronisation is checked. The magnetic compass can be read from the bridge through a periscope or reflector.
Transducer (dönüştürücü), elektrik enerj: The transducer converts electrical energy into a sound pulse; the pulse travels to the seabed, is reflected and returns. The depth is calculated from the round-trip time and the speed of sound in water (≈1500 m/s): D = (c·t)/2. The result is shown on the display and as a recording (echo trace).
Echo sounder derinliği transducer'dan öl: The echo sounder measures depth from the transducer. The value shown on the display can be set with an offset to refer to the transducer, the bottom of the keel or the water surface. For assessing UKC, the reference must be clearly known.
Yumuşak çamur tabanda zayıf yankı, yoğun: A weak echo from a soft mud bottom, a dense shoal of fish or a thermocline layer can show a wrong depth. A multiple echo can appear as a multiple of the real depth. In shallow and critical waters the echo sounder reading is cross-checked with other sources (chart, draft).
UKC (karina altı boşluk), squat, gel-git: UKC (under-keel clearance) changes with squat, tide, waves and salinity. The echo sounder shows the real-time clearance under the keel, which is compared with the planned UKC. It is monitored continuously when navigating in shallow water and the alarm is set appropriately.
SOLAS V/19, derinlik ölçüm cihazı taşıma: SOLAS V/19 makes it mandatory to carry an echo-sounding device. The shallow water alarm gives an audible and visual warning when the depth falls below the selected safe depth; it is kept active on the bridge.
Dikey tip (vertical shaft) windlass, zin: In a vertical-shaft windlass, the chain wheel (wildcat/gypsy) is on deck and the drive mechanism is in a compartment below deck. It saves space on the forecastle and is preferred on large merchant ships.
Yatay tip (horizontal shaft) windlass, t: In a horizontal-shaft windlass all components are on deck. It makes maintenance easier and is common on medium-sized ships.
Kombine windlass/mooring winch, hem zinc: A combined windlass/mooring winch has both the chain wheel and a rope drum on the same shaft. It saves space and cost.
Elektrik tahrikli windlass: AC veya DC m: Electrically driven windlass: works with an AC or DC motor. Speed control is easy. It is used on most modern ships.
Hidrolik tahrikli windlass: Hidrolik pom: Hydraulically driven windlass: works with a hydraulic pump and motor. High torque capacity, compact size and overload protection are its advantages. It is common on tankers and bulk carriers.
Elektro-hidrolik windlass, elektrik moto: An electro-hydraulic windlass works with a hydraulic motor or cylinder supplied by a hydraulic pump driven by an electric motor.
Windlass kapasitesi Equipment Number (EN: The windlass capacity is determined by the Equipment Number (EN). The EN depends on the ship's displacement, its height above the waterline (freeboard plus superstructures and deckhouses) and its lateral area.
Tek bumbalı jib vinç: En yaygın gemi vin: Single-jib crane: the most common type of ship's crane. It may be electro-hydraulic or fully electric. It has hoisting, luffing and slewing movements.
Çift bumbalı vinç: İki bumba ile daha ge: Twin-jib crane: gives a wider working area with two jibs.
Gantry crane (portal vinç): Konteyner ge: Gantry crane: a crane that travels over the hatch covers on container ships. It gives high speed and precise positioning.
Derrick (çubuk bumba): Eski tip gemilerd: Derrick: a lifting arrangement seen on older ships that works with a derrick boom and ropes. With the union purchase method, two derricks are worked together for fast operation.
Safe Working Load (SWL), onaylı yük diya: The Safe Working Load (SWL) is the upper limit permitted for the boom angle/radius and working arrangement in the approved load diagram; the weights of the hook block, spreader and loose gear are taken into account.
Muayene, kapsamlı muayene ve proof-load: The scope of inspections, thorough examinations and proof load tests is not taken from a fixed table found on the internet; it is verified from the flag state's requirements, SOLAS II-1/3-13, MSC.1/Circ.1663, the applicability of ILO Convention 152 and the ship's Register of Lifting Appliances/Cargo Gear Book.
Head line: Baş taraftan rıhtıma ileriye: Head line: a line leading forward from the bow to the quay. It holds the ship in towards the quay.
Stern line: Kıç taraftan rıhtıma geriye: Stern line: a line leading aft from the stern to the quay.
Breast line: Gemiden rıhtıma dik olarak: Breast line: a line leading from the ship to the quay at right angles. It keeps the ship close to the quay.
Spring line: Gemiden rıhtıma boylamasına: Spring line: a line leading from the ship to the quay in a fore-and-aft direction. A spring leading forward prevents the ship from moving aft, and a spring leading aft prevents it from moving forward.
Halat türleri: Polipropilen (PP), poliam: Types of rope: polypropylene (PP), polyamide (nylon), polyester, HMPE (Dyneema) and wire rope. The different types have different elongation and breaking properties; using them mixed is dangerous.
Gergin halat koptuğunda depolanan enerji: When a line under tension parts, the stored energy is released and the line snaps back. In line with OCIMF recommendations, snap-back zones are marked on deck.
Sentetik halatlar tel halatlardan çok da: Synthetic ropes store much more energy than wire ropes and are much more dangerous when they part. Snap-back is the leading cause of deaths in mooring operations.
Otomatik gerilim özellikli vinçler, hala: Winches with automatic tensioning keep the line tension at the set value. They compensate for the effects of tide, changes in loading and wind.
Hidrolik veya frekans kontrollü elektrik: They work with a hydraulic or frequency-controlled electric motor. A tension sensor (load cell) measures the line force continuously.
Kauçuk contalar (rubber packing), compre: The rubber packing, compression bars, cross-joints and drains together provide weathertight integrity; renewing only the packing does not correct a misaligned panel or poorly adjusted cleats.
Hose test: Onaylı test düzenine göre dış: Hose test: water is applied from outside according to the approved test arrangement and ingress is watched for from inside; the water pressure, nozzle distance and rate of travel are not chosen at random.
Ultrasonic test: Daha güvenilir bir yönt: Ultrasonic test: a more reliable method in which the tightness of the packing is measured with an ultrasonic transmitter inside the hold and a receiver outside.
Tebeşir testi: Contaya tebeşir sürülerek: Chalk test: chalk is applied to the compression bar and the cover is closed; when the cover is opened, the chalk mark on the packing must be evenly distributed.
Capstan, windlass'tan farklı olarak yaln: Unlike a windlass, a capstan is used only for heaving on ropes; it has no chain-holding function. The rope is wound a few turns around the vertical barrel and heaved by friction.
Elektrik veya hidrolik tahriklidir. Baş: It is electrically or hydraulically driven and located on the forecastle and poop deck. It is used for heaving mooring lines and for warping.
Capstan tamburuna sarılan halattaki sürt: The friction force in a rope wound around the capstan barrel is calculated with Euler's formula.
Bollard: a fixed post to which a line is made fast. It may be single, double or T-type. Its SWL is marked on it.
Fairlead (panama chock): Halatı yönlendi: Fairlead (Panama chock): a guide used to lead the line. It may be of the roller or closed type.
Pedestal roller: Halat yönlendirme makar: Pedestal roller: a roller for leading a line. It reduces friction.
Bitts: İkili bağlama babası. Halat 8 şek: Bitts: a double mooring post. The line is made fast in figure-of-eight turns.
Magnetronlu veya solid-state verici, sca: A magnetron or solid-state transmitter sends electromagnetic energy through the scanner. The round-trip time of the echo returning from a target gives the range; the azimuth position of the antenna gives the relative bearing. When the gyro heading is added, true bearings and a north-up/course-up presentation can be produced.
Receiver ve signal processor çok zayıf e: The receiver and signal processor amplify very weak echoes while trying to suppress sea clutter, rain clutter and interference. Excessive use of the gain or clutter controls can remove not only the noise but also real targets such as a small craft, a buoy, a low coastline or a target between the waves.
Radarın operasyonel değeri yalnız ekoyu: The operational value of the radar is not only that it shows echoes: the correct choice of presentation and motion, a suitable range scale, EBL/VRM measurement, parallel indexing, trails and ARPA target tracking are different layers of evidence in the same picture.
X-band yaklaşık 9 GHz/3 cm dalga boyunda: X-band works at about 9 GHz / 3 cm wavelength; it gives high discrimination of small targets and coastal detail and triggers radar SARTs, but it can be more affected by precipitation. S-band is at about 3 GHz / 10 cm wavelength; it can give a more stable long-range picture in heavy precipitation and some sea conditions, but it does not show the classic radar SART response.
İki radar varsa aynı ayar ve range'de ko: If there are two radars, they should not be used like copies of each other with the same settings and range. Independent pictures that reduce common blind spots are created with different bands, ranges, pulse/presentation and clutter settings.
Önce brilliance/contrast ve background,: First the brilliance/contrast and background are set, then a suitable range scale, orientation and motion are selected. Unstabilised head-up gives a simple relative picture; gyro-stabilised course-up or north-up makes comparison with the chart and true bearings easier. Relative motion and true motion are the movement reference of the whole radar picture, not of the target vectors.
Gain, boş alanda hafif speckle görülecek: The gain is checked manually by turning it back slightly from the level at which a light speckle appears in an empty area. Sea clutter suppresses wave echoes close to the ship; rain clutter suppresses precipitation cells. The controls are kept at the lowest level necessary and re-checked on different ranges to make sure small targets have not disappeared.
Kısa pulse yakın hedef ayrımını, uzun pu: A short pulse supports the discrimination of close targets, a long pulse / suitable processing supports the energy returned from distant targets. Pulse compression and auto modes on solid-state equipment are specific to the maker; the user must know from the display which automatic function is active.
Shadow/blind sector; mast, baca, crane v: A shadow or blind sector is where targets on certain bearings are weakened or lost because of masts, funnels, cranes or cargo. These sectors are managed with the bridge poster and inspection information and with the other radar and a visual lookout.
Side-lobe, multiple echo, indirect echo,: Side-lobe echoes, multiple echoes, indirect echoes, second-trace echoes and interference can look like real targets. They are distinguished by their movement relative to fixed objects, their behaviour when the range is changed, and by checking with another radar and visually.
Ducting, yoğun yağış, sea state, hedef r: Ducting, heavy precipitation, the sea state, the target's radar cross-section and the antenna height change the detection range. A target beyond the radar horizon or with a low RCS not being visible does not mean the target is not there.
EBL/VRM ile ölçülen bearing/range; curso: Bearings and ranges measured with the EBL/VRM give quantitative evidence for decisions, rather than the cursor or an estimate by eye on the screen. If relative bearings are used, gyro/heading error and the own ship's heading reference are dealt with separately.
Parallel index, sabit bir radar objesini: Parallel indexing shows the cross-track situation by following the movement of a fixed radar object against a planned PI line; it is not a copy of the electronic route line. The PI is prepared with a suitable radar-conspicuous object, the correct range and bearing, and clearing distances calculated in the passage plan.
Bir sabit objenin EBL bearing trendi, ra: The EBL bearing trend of a fixed object supports checks of the radar bearing alignment and the compass error. Because the radar overlay alignment may share the same GNSS/gyro error, it does not count on its own as an independent position check.
ARPA ardışık radar ölçümlerinden hedef t: ARPA builds a target track from successive radar measurements; with the own ship's heading and speed input it produces relative and true course and speed, and CPA and TCPA estimates. The solution may be unstable for a newly acquired target, a target that is manoeuvring, one whose echo merges with another, or one that stays in clutter.
Relative vector, mevcut hareketler sürer: The relative vector shows the path the target will follow relative to the own ship if present movements continue; the true vector shows its actual direction and speed relative to the selected ground or water speed reference. Looking only at the tip of the arrow without reading the vector mode and time leads to a wrong interpretation of a manoeuvre.
Trial manoeuvre karar desteğidir; gecikm: The trial manoeuvre is a decision aid; it depends on the delay time, the planned course or speed change and the assumption that the targets keep their present tracks. The result does not take over the responsibility under COLREG, the visual lookout or the bridge team's assessment.
Rule 5 tüm uygun araçlarla gözcülük; Rul: Rule 5 requires a lookout by all available means; Rule 6 a safe speed; Rule 7 determining risk of collision with all available means; Rule 8 early, substantial and safe action to avoid collision. A bearing that remains steady or does not change appreciably, together with a decreasing range, is a sign of serious risk; at close range risk may exist even if the bearing changes.
Kısıtlı görüşte Rule 19 uygulanır. Radar: In restricted visibility Rule 19 applies. Whether a radar target is forward of or abaft the beam, the risk of a close-quarters situation and the direction of the course alteration are considered together; a COLREG manoeuvre is not based only on an AIS name or a VHF agreement.
Radar plotting bir defalık CPA okuması d: Radar plotting is not a single reading of the CPA. The target is acquired, the solution is allowed to settle, the bearing, range and vector trends are followed, and the effect of any manoeuvre made is checked again after a sufficient time.
Performance monitor/BITE sonucu, sea ret: The performance monitor/BITE result, the sea return and the appearance of known radar-conspicuous objects are the daily evidence of operational performance. On magnetron systems the warm-up and tuning behaviour, and on solid-state systems the self-test and module status, are followed according to the maker's manual.
Heading/speed input kaybında radar ekosu: When the heading or speed input is lost, radar echoes may still be present but the stabilisation and the reliability of the ARPA true data are lost. The user isolates the faulty layer, reverts to relative measurements and manual plotting or other radar and visual methods, informs the Master and records the fault.
Radar arızasında hedefi 'onarım yaparak': When a radar fails, the first duty of the officer of the watch is not to "repair" it but to make the situation operationally safe with a safe speed, an additional lookout, an alternative radar or navigation sensor and, if necessary, a change of route or area.
ECDIS carriage requirement tüm SOLAS gem: The ECDIS carriage requirement is not the same for all SOLAS ships; the ship type, GT, date of build and applicable transitional provisions are verified from the Record of Equipment. The carriage requirement and the back-up arrangement are also separate matters: a second independent ECDIS, an up-to-date paper folio or another adequate arrangement accepted by the Administration is defined in the ship's approved documentation.
ECDIS ancak resmî Hydrographic Office ye: An ECDIS provides the legal chart function only when it is used with up-to-date ENCs/ENDS issued under the authority of an official Hydrographic Office and in an approved operating mode. An ECS, a web chart, a pilot application or an unofficial chart does not meet the SOLAS chart carriage requirement, even if it appears on the ECDIS screen.
RNC'nin bulunduğu RCDS modunda ECDIS'in: In RCDS mode, where RNCs are used, the vector alarm and query capabilities of the ECDIS are reduced. RCDS use is managed together with the required up-to-date paper charts and the procedure for the flag and route concerned; opening a raster chart on the screen does not automatically give legal equivalence.
Legacy ECDIS'te resmî vektör ENC esas ol: On legacy ECDIS, official vector ENCs are distributed mainly in the IHO S-57 transfer standard; they are loaded through the S-63 data protection/permit mechanism and converted losslessly into the maker's internal SENC format. The symbols, colours and display categories on the screen follow the IHO S-52 Presentation Library and the equipment performance standard.
S-101, S-100 tabanlı yeni nesil ENC ürün: S-101 is the next-generation ENC product based on S-100 and cannot be opened on every existing S-57 ECDIS. MSC.530(106) accepts either MSC.232(82) or the new standard for equipment installed between 1 January 2026 and 31 December 2028; ECDIS installed from 1 January 2029 will comply with the new, S-100-capable standard. This does not mean that all ships' ENCs switch to S-101 overnight.
Base cell, new edition ve incremental up: The sequence of base cells, new editions and incremental updates, permit validity, the update log and rejections, and presentation library/software compatibility are checked together. Updates are applied as they are issued by the official service; although most services use a weekly package, "pressing a button once a week" is not the only evidence that the charts are up to date.
Passage appraisal, kalkıştan varışa ve c: The passage appraisal checks, from departure to arrival and to the contingency and abort ports, the official ENC coverage, the appropriate usage band and compilation scale, the permits, the latest updates, services such as the T&P/AVCS information overlay, and the required nautical publications.
Overscale, underscale, no data, better-s: The overscale, underscale, no data, better-scale ENC available and datum shift indications are read for what they mean. Zooming in does not create new detail; when the source/compilation scale is exceeded, positions and object geometry can give a false sense of precision.
CATZOC/quality of bathymetric data ve so: CATZOC/quality of bathymetric data and the source diagram describe the survey quality and uncertainty of the depth information; safe water is not as certain as the "blue-white colour". In UKC and route decisions this quality is assessed together with squat, tide and the ship's motion.
Safety depth, spot sounding'lerin vurgul: The safety depth is the threshold at which spot soundings are highlighted; it is not an alarm limit on its own. If there is no contour equal to the user value, the next deeper contour available in the ENC is selected as the safety contour; it is used as the boundary between safe and unsafe water and feeds the crossing/approach warning logic.
Shallow ve deep contour esas olarak renk: The shallow and deep contours mainly arrange the colour bands and situational awareness. The XTD is the route corridor; it may differ on each leg according to channel width, traffic, positioning accuracy, bank and turning effects and the abort area. The look-ahead (time or distance sector) depends on the maker's interface and is set according to the ship's actual stopping and turning needs.
Safety settings şirket UKC politikası ve: The safety settings are derived from the company UKC policy and the Master-approved passage plan. Squat, heel/list, wave response/density allowance, the required UKC and the height of tide are added to the static draft with a clear sign convention; the single draft field in the ECDIS does not do this calculation on its own.
Route, berth-to-berth hazırlanır; waypoi: The route is prepared berth to berth; waypoints and legs, turn radius and wheel-over, the speed plan, XTD, clearing ranges/PI, reporting points, no-go and limiting danger lines, abort points, contingency anchorages and pilotage notes are linked in a single passage plan.
Automatic route check seçili safety cont: The automatic route check gives warnings based on the selected safety contour and mariner's objects, but it cannot be relied on to catch objects off the screen, a wrong display or scale, user charts, T&P information, chart quality or shortcomings in the software interpretation. Zero warnings is not a certificate of a safe route.
OOW rotayı appropriate largest scale/usa: The OOW reviews the route visually leg by leg on the appropriate largest scale/usage band, resolves and justifies every alarm and indication, and uses it as a protected route after the Master's approval. A last-minute route revision goes through the same chain of appraisal, check, visual review and approval.
Monitoring modunda active route/leg, cro: In monitoring mode, the active route and leg, cross-track distance, next waypoint and turn, the selected position, heading and speed sensors, the chart scale and the alarms are monitored at the same time. If there is a track-control/autopilot connection, mode awareness and readiness for manual takeover are particularly maintained.
Primary GNSS position, mümkün olan bağım: The primary GNSS position is cross-checked with a second independent PNT source where possible and with radar, visual or terrestrial fixes. Two ECDIS units using the same GNSS, gyro and log are not two independent checks. The radar overlay also often shares the same heading and position input.
Manual fix yalnız sembol koymak değil; s: A manual fix is not just placing a symbol; it is a record of the source, time, accuracy and any discrepancy. When a position jump or freeze, spoofing or jamming, a datum mismatch or a misalignment of charted objects is seen, reliance on track control is stopped, the Master is called and the safe speed and sea room are reassessed.
Alarm, warning ve caution/indication üre: Alarms, warnings and cautions/indications may have different priorities and sound behaviour depending on the maker and the applicable performance standard. Acknowledging only manages the sound; it does not remove the danger or the sensor failure. Alarms are not silenced in bulk without reading the alarm list, the source and the consequence.
Alarm yorgunluğu çoğunlukla yanlış safet: Alarm fatigue mostly comes from wrong safety settings, unnecessary user layers, an unsuitable look-ahead or XTD, or unresolved chart objects. The solution is not to desensitise the system but to correct the passage plan and the settings for the operational context.
Over-reliance yalnız pencereden dışarı b: Over-reliance is not only failing to look out of the window: accepting the automatic route check as absolute, believing two screens fed from the same source are independent, thinking that zooming in on the chart increases accuracy and reading a predicted position as a measured fix are also examples of over-reliance.
ECDIS failure; black screen kadar positi: An ECDIS failure is not only a black screen; it can also be a loss of the position or heading source, frozen data, a corrupted SENC, a permit or update failure, a wrong time, network lag, unsafe settings, or the back-up unit being exposed to the same common-mode failure.
Backup arrangement primary ECDIS arızala: The back-up arrangement must be ready for use the moment the primary ECDIS fails, it must be up to date, and the method of transferring or recreating the passage plan must be known. If the second ECDIS is affected by the same switchboard, GNSS or network failure, its real independence is addressed in the company risk assessment.
Arızada OOW önce seyri emniyete alır: ma: In a failure the OOW first makes the navigation safe: manual steering or an appropriate mode, a safe speed, an additional lookout and more frequent fixes, an alternative chart or navigation method, and calling the Master. A reboot or service work is carried out according to the maker and the SMS once the navigational risk is under control.
STCW'ye göre ECDIS kullanan zabit gerekl: Under STCW, an officer using ECDIS must have the required generic ECDIS competence. On joining a ship, familiarisation with that maker and model, the menu logic, alarms, route transfer, sensor selection and the back-up is required under the ISM/SMS. In any case it should not be written as if a separate, uniform international certificate called a "type-specific certificate" were mandatory; flag and company requirements are checked separately.
1 Ocak 2026-2028 arasında yeni kurulan E: ECDIS newly installed between 1 January 2026 and 2028 may comply with the MSC.232(82) or the MSC.530(106) family; new installations from 1 January 2029 move to the revised standard that supports the S-100 product family. The user should know the type-approval baseline and the software/presentation library version of their own equipment from the service records.
Class A taşıma zorunluluğu 'tüm SOLAS ge: The Class A carriage requirement cannot be generalised as "all SOLAS ships"; it is verified against the ship type, type of voyage and GT thresholds in SOLAS V/19 and the Record of Equipment. Class A makes higher-priority reports based on SOTDMA.
Class B, ilgili ulusal kurallar veya gön: Class B may be found on small commercial ships and craft under the relevant national rules or as voluntary equipment. The power, access method and reporting interval vary with the sub-class of the equipment.
AIS sürekli açık tutulmalıdır; kaptan gü: AIS must be kept switched on at all times; the Master may switch it off for safety or security reasons, but this decision must be recorded in the log book.
AIS verileri tek başına çatışma önleme k: AIS data must not be used on its own for collision avoidance decisions; it must be assessed together with radar and a visual lookout.
MMSI numarası bayrak devleti tarafından: The MMSI number is assigned by the flag state and is unique.
GPS, en az 4 uydudan gelen sinyal ile al: GPS calculates the receiver's position and time from the signals of at least 4 satellites. Each satellite broadcasts its own position and the time the signal was sent. The receiver calculates the range from the time the signal takes to arrive.
Gösterilen fix kalitesi; uydu geometrisi: The quality of the fix shown depends on satellite geometry, the antenna's view of the sky, the ionosphere, multipath, integrity monitoring and the augmentation used. A single "± metres" value does not prove the reliability of the position at that moment.
Differential GPS, kıyı istasyonlarından: Differential GPS improves accuracy with correction data received from shore stations. It is important in port approaches and coastal navigation.
SBAS (Satellite Based Augmentation Syste: SBAS (Satellite Based Augmentation System): satellite-based correction systems such as WAAS (USA), EGNOS (Europe) and MSAS (Japan) improve accuracy regionally.
Jiroskopik prensiple çalışan pusula, dün: A compass working on the gyroscopic principle aligns itself with the earth's axis of rotation and points to true north. Its error (gyro error) is small and can be corrected.
Fiber optik jiroskop (FOG) ve ring laser: The fibre optic gyroscope (FOG) and the ring laser gyroscope (RLG) are modern solid-state types. They have no moving parts and are more reliable.
Gyro pusula tekrarlayıcıları (repeater): Gyro compass repeaters are located on the bridge, the bridge wings and in the steering gear compartment.
Manyetik pusula, gemideki demir ve çelik: The magnetic compass has a deviation error caused by the iron and steel structures of the ship. This error is corrected with the Flinders bar, soft-iron spheres and magnets (compass adjustment).
Variation (iğne sapması) coğrafi konuma: Variation depends on the geographical position and is read from the chart. It has an annual change.
Toplam hata = Variation + Deviation. CDM: Total error = variation + deviation. The CDMVT rule: Compass → Deviation → Magnetic → Variation → True.
Transducer, ses darbesi gönderir ve deni: The transducer sends a sound pulse and receives the echo reflected from the seabed. The depth is calculated from the round-trip time.
Suda ses hızı sıcaklık, tuzluluk ve bası: The speed of sound in water varies with temperature, salinity and pressure. Standard calibration assumes 1500 m/s, but the actual value may vary between 1450 and 1540 m/s.
Bar check: Transducer altına bilinen der: Bar check: the echo sounder is calibrated by lowering a metal plate to a known depth below the transducer.
İki zamanlı motorda her krank mili dönüş: In a two-stroke engine there is one power stroke for every crankshaft revolution. As the piston descends it uncovers the ports, and the scavenge air drives the burnt gases out of the cylinder and fills it with fresh air.
Uniflow scavenging: Hava alttan girer, e: Uniflow scavenging: the air enters at the bottom and the exhaust leaves through the exhaust valve at the top. It is the standard method on modern two-stroke engines.
Crosshead yapısı sayesinde piston kolu v: With the crosshead design, the piston rod and the connecting rod are joined at the crosshead pin; the piston moves only vertically. As a result, cylinder lubrication and crankcase lubrication are separate.
Common-rail, elektronik-hidrolik veya ka: Common-rail, electronic-hydraulic or cam-driven mechanical injection may be used. Rail/servo and injection pressures vary with the load point and engine design; alarm/trip and maintenance limits are taken only from the maker's manual and shop trial data.
VIT (Variable Injection Timing): Yük dur: VIT (Variable Injection Timing): the injection timing is changed according to the load. Early injection at low loads and late injection at high loads give optimum combustion.
Dört zamanlı motorda emme, sıkıştırma, i: A four-stroke engine has four strokes: intake, compression, power and exhaust. There is one power stroke every two crankshaft revolutions.
Trunk piston tasarımı kullanılır; crossh: A trunk piston design is used; there is no crosshead. The engine is more compact and lighter, but the power per cylinder is lower than that of a two-stroke engine.
Turbocharger ile doldurulan hava, interc: The air charged by the turbocharger is cooled in the intercooler and delivered to the intake manifold.
Krank mili → Ara şaft (intermediate shaf: Crankshaft → intermediate shaft → thrust bearing → propeller shaft → propeller.
İtme yatağı (Michell tipi): Tilting pad: Thrust bearing (Michell type): transfers the propeller thrust to the ship's structure with a tilting-pad bearing design. It runs on an oil film.
Stern tube: Pervane şaftının gemi gövdes: Stern tube: provides bearing support and sealing where the propeller shaft leaves the hull.
Flanşlı kaplin: Şaft segmentlerini birbi: Flanged coupling: connects the shaft sections to each other.
Şaft hizalaması lazer alignment veya sag: Shaft alignment is done by laser alignment or the sag-and-gap method. Misalignment can cause bearing wear, vibration and shaft fracture.
Torsional vibration (burulma titreşimi):: Torsional vibration: a periodic twisting moment caused by the cylinders of the engine firing at different times. Resonance can occur at critical speeds; a barred speed range is defined.
Pervane kanat yüzeyinde yerel basıncın s: Cavitation is the collapse of vapour bubbles formed when the local pressure on the propeller blade surface falls below the vapour pressure of the water. It causes erosion, noise, vibration and a loss of efficiency.
Kavitasyon türleri: Sheet (yüzey), tip v: Types of cavitation: sheet, tip vortex, bubble, cloud and supercavitation.
Kavitasyonu azaltmak için kanat profili: To reduce cavitation, the blade profile is optimised, the blade tips are shaped and the propeller is loaded appropriately.
Elektrik motoru ile tahrik edilen hidrol: A hydraulic pump driven by an electric motor sends pressurised oil to the steering cylinders. Rapson slide or rotary vane type actuators are used.
Güç ünitesi, kontrol devresi ve ayrım dü: The power units, control circuits and separation arrangements are approved according to the size of the ship and the applicable paragraphs of SOLAS II-1/29. Seeing two pumps is not on its own proof of full independence.
Ana steering gear için yaygın SOLAS krit: The usual SOLAS criterion for the main steering gear is to put the rudder over from 35° on one side to 35° on the other side at the deepest draft and maximum ahead service speed, and in any case from 35° on either side to 30° on the other side in not more than 28 seconds.
Auxiliary steering gear için kriter, yin: The criterion for the auxiliary steering gear is to put the rudder over from 15° on one side to 15° on the other side in not more than 60 seconds, again at the defined draft and at one half of the maximum ahead service speed or 7 knots, whichever is greater; exceptions and equivalent arrangements are checked in the approved documents.
Yardımcı dizel motor genellikle dört zam: The auxiliary diesel engine is usually a four-stroke, medium-speed engine. It runs at constant speed to produce 50 Hz or 60 Hz power, for example 720 or 900 rpm for 60 Hz (750 or 1000 rpm for 50 Hz).
Alternatör, 3 fazlı AC gerilim üretir. G: The alternator produces three-phase AC voltage. The ship's main busbar voltage is usually 440 V or 6.6 kV.
İki jeneratörü aynı baraya bağlamak için: To connect two generators to the same busbar, their frequency, voltage, phase sequence and phase angle must be equal.
Synchroscope veya synchronizing lamps il: The phase match is checked with the synchroscope or synchronising lamps. The breaker is closed as the synchroscope pointer approaches the 12 o'clock position.
Otomatik senkronizasyon sistemleri freka: Automatic synchronising systems adjust the frequency and voltage difference automatically and close the breaker at the right moment.
Paralel çalışan jeneratörler arasında ak: Between generators in parallel, active power (kW) is shared through the governor setting and reactive power (kVAR) through the AVR (Automatic Voltage Regulator) setting.
Droop mode: Her jeneratörün frekansı yük: Droop mode: the frequency of each generator falls slightly as the load increases; this gives natural load sharing.
Isochronous mode: Frekans sabit tutulur;: Isochronous mode: the frequency is kept constant; the load is shared equally by the load sharing controller.
pH, alkalinite, iletkenlik/TDS, klorür,: The targets for pH, alkalinity, conductivity/TDS, chloride, phosphate and oxygen scavenger are set according to the boiler pressure, the metallurgy and the treatment programme used. A single range taken from the internet does not apply to all boilers.
Klorür trendi condenser/deniz suyu kaçağ: A chloride trend can show a condenser or seawater leak; the acceptance and blowdown limits are the values of the water treatment supplier and the maker's manual.
Sertlik ve besi suyu kontaminasyonu scal: Hardness and feed water contamination create a risk of scale and overheating; the measurement method and the corrective step are recorded according to the test kit procedure.
Kimyasal seçimi gelişigüzel yapılmaz; ba: Chemicals are not chosen at random; some oxygen scavengers have health and environmental restrictions. They are dosed only according to the approved treatment programme and the SDS.
Emniyet valfi: Kazan basıncı ayar değeri: Safety valve: opens automatically when the boiler pressure exceeds the set value. There must be at least two.
Su seviye alarmı: Düşük su seviyesi (low: Water level alarm: the low water level alarm and the low-low water level trip.
Alev gözü (flame eye): Brülör alevini iz: Flame eye: monitors the burner flame; if the flame goes out, the fuel is cut off.
Kapak kilitleme (interlock): Furnace kap: Door interlock: the burner cannot operate while the furnace door is open.
Santrifüj kuvvet, ağır partikülleri dışa: Centrifugal force throws the heavy particles outwards. The disc stack increases the separating surface. The bowl rotates at 6000–9000 rpm.
Purifier: separates both water and solids. The position of the interface is controlled by the gravity disc (dam ring).
Clarifier: Yalnızca katı partikülleri ay: Clarifier: separates only solid particles; there is no water outlet.
Gravity disc çapı, yakıtın yoğunluğuna g: The diameter of the gravity disc is chosen according to the density of the fuel. Choosing the wrong disc causes fuel to escape through the water outlet or water to mix with the fuel.
HFO arıtma sırası: Settling tank → Purif: HFO treatment sequence: settling tank → purifier → clarifier → service tank → engine.
